findings.location: ## Definition, lines 25–36 (real and normalized-complex densities; product law)
findings.evidence: The batch-11 Definition states the real and normalized-complex density formulas, declares all expectations to be integrals against their product density, and asserts E|z|^2=1. Its declared dependency closure supplies Countable Choice and Lebesgue measure but no density-normalization or moment result. The assigned consumer lem-gaussian-squared-norm-tail uses F1 as a probability density and step 1.1 asserts the prefactored integral is one. The local lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one assumes full AC, stronger than this definition's Countable Choice assumption; thm-gaussian-integral and lem-plane-gaussian-integral-in-polar-coordinates are not in the definition's dependency closure, and the normalized-complex law still needs a local normalization and moment argument under the stated assumption. The cited HMT §10.1 focuses on real standard Gaussian matrices and says complex analogues hold; MT §11.4.2 analyzes real standard-normal test matrices. Neither cited passage provides the local normalized-complex density proof. A local proof under Countable Choice or a compatible proved supplier is needed.
